## Selected research


```{=html}
<div class="work-list"><article class="work-card"><p class="eyebrow">2026 · Cambridge Journal of Artificial Intelligence</p><h3><a href="/publications/epistemic_frontier_capitalism/">The Epistemic Frontier of Capitalism: A Theory of Epistemic Regression through Artificial Intelligence and Misinformation</a></h3><p>This article argues that contemporary capitalism has entered a phase in which outcomes are increasingly shaped by the privatization and strategic destabilization of the epistemic commons through frontier artificial intelligence and platform-mediated misinformation.</p><a class="text-link" href="/publications/epistemic_frontier_capitalism/">Read more <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></article><article class="work-card"><p class="eyebrow">2026 · Review of Evolutionary Political Economy</p><h3><a href="/publications/liberal_order_complex_societies_climate_change/">The liberal order in complex societies marred by climate change</a></h3><p>This essay develops a complexity-oriented research program for classical liberal thought, showing how rule-of-law institutions can enable cooperation amid political, economic, and environmental pressures from climate change.</p><a class="text-link" href="/publications/liberal_order_complex_societies_climate_change/">Read more <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></article><article class="work-card"><p class="eyebrow">2026 · PLOS Climate</p><h3><a href="/publications/Beyond_post_truth_climate_misinformation/">Beyond post-truth: Projecting the future trajectory of climate misinformation</a></h3><p>Climate misinformation represents one of the most significant barriers to effective climate action in the 21st century. Building upon Yotam Ophir’s framework, this essay examines how climate misinformation is evolving and projects its future trajectory.</p><a class="text-link" href="/publications/Beyond_post_truth_climate_misinformation/">Read more <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></article></div>
```

<p class="section-more"><a class="text-link" href="/publications/">All publications & working papers →</a></p><section class="about-section" id="about"><div><p class="eyebrow">The researcher</p><h2>Across disciplines.<br>Focused on the world.</h2></div><div><p>I am a PhD candidate in the Department of Government at The University of Essex on the <a href="https://www.essex.ac.uk/postgraduate/research/doctoral-training-partnerships/sustainable-transitions">Leverhulme Sustainable Transitions Doctoral Training Programme</a>.</p><p>My research interests include quantitative social science, political economy and misinformation, and environmental governance. My PhD research project, primarily supervised by Dr. Zorzeta Bakaki in the  <a href="https://www.essex.ac.uk/departments/government">Department of Government</a>, is on the political, social, and economic effects of climate change misinformation.</p><p>While my primary discipline is political science, the Essex Sustainable Transitions programme is interdisciplinary in scope, and I have a secondary supervisor, Professor Thankom Arun, in the <a href="https://www.essex.ac.uk/departments/essex-business-school">Essex Business School</a>.</p><p>I am a Policy Fellow at the <a href="https://ccod.co.uk">Council for Countering Online Disinformation</a>, an Affiliate of the <a href="https://sticerd.lse.ac.uk/_new/programmes/hayek/">Hayek Programme in Liberal Political Economy</a> at the London School of Economics, a Research Fellow at the <a href="https://www.earthsystemgovernance.org/person/james-kennon-rice/">Earth System Governance Project</a>, a Ronald Coase Fellow at <a href="https://www.mercatus.org/students/ronald-coase-fellows">The Mercatus Center</a> at George Mason University, and I was formerly a Research Associate with the <a href="https://www.politics.ox.ac.uk/oxford-computational-political-science-group">Oxford Computational Political Science Group</a> (OCPSG), based in Oxford University's <a href="https://www.politics.ox.ac.uk">Department of Politics and International Relations</a>.</p></div></section><aside class="news-note"><p class="eyebrow">Currently</p><p><strong>Call for papers:</strong> I am guest editing, with Bryan Cheang, a Cosmos + Taxis special issue on <em>Misinformation, Synthetic Media, and Digital Literacy in the Age of AI</em>.
